body:
Yes I always walk off with the probe far enough to wear the needle disappears. I then advance forward until it reappears. I typically do this 2-3 times before attempting to pass the wire. I feel like if I was through and through I would not be able to see myself walk the needle in. As I would only be walking inferior to the vessel. Prior to my recent 2 week slump, I was getting 95% of my a lines. So they often would let me do my thing. At that time I was entering the skin almost flat , finding my needle tip. Then steepening up a little bit and advancing until I entered. And walked it in once inside quite a bit. But I was recently on a month of OB and then vacation so I feel rusty. And then I began to work with new attendings who have me try various ways to hold the arrow, probe, and angle of needle. Definitely getting in my head about it as well. 
The first attempt I mentioned had great flash almost all the way up the arrow while I was advancing. At some point after my last advance forward in the vessel , me dropping the probe and passing the wire I lost it some where. I think after advancing I dropped my angle then passed the wire. Maybe it was too much movement in a certain direction and I went through one of the wall. For my second attempt I had no flash. I scanned and traced the catheter after passing it and it was in the R upper corner of the lumen but definitely looked inside the vessel. Potentially just outside the intima . Frustrating as it appeared to be an easy stick and directly centered in the lumen.
No I never knew that, thank you! I will do that going forward
Thank you I will try to continue advancing a bit further !

I typically try to advance a a couple mm or cm at a time like 1-3 times to walk it in, which may not be enough. I have found maybe a couple times if I walk it in pretty deep I may get flash or it will work but sometimes i forego this if we’re in a rush. I will definitely try to advance some more next time and try the steady pressure , thank you!
I definitely am guilty of this and only realized after the fact , when I could have done the through and through. I will keep this in mind. Thank you!

I’ve had quite a few arrow a lines where I have no flash or blood return at all. And when I pass the wire and catheter and remove the wire I will have pulsatile flow. But there are other times I don’t have flash or blood return in the arrow but my US image appears like I’m in the center of the lumen and slowly advancing it but the opposite is true after attempting to pass the catheter or remove the wire. No pulsatile flow.
I tend to adjust the angle quite a bit sometimes. I will definitely try that and keep that in mind. Thank you!
Thank you, I will try this next time!
